feedback.text: They should show the recruit page on the left, like we made consistent for everything else. The pages underneath should be very similar to the roster in the way that it's done, except it's the recruit player page, not the roster player page. It should be very clear at the top that this is underneath the recruitment. This is /recruitment, not /roster. — DONE on W2-01: Recruitment is selected in the sidebar, the page is built card-for-card on the shipped player record, the line under the name reads "Recruitment · 2026-27", the route is /operate/recruitment/<recruit> and the button at the foot reads BACK TO RECRUITMENT.

We shouldn't invent UI elements here. We should see what the roster is, and we should see the player and all the stuff there. — DONE: every card is a shipped card. PERSON kept; ONBOARDING becomes RECRUITMENT; SEASON becomes THE RECRUIT-STAGE ASK; the shipped ATTENDANCE table becomes RECRUITMENT EVENTS unchanged in kind; THEIR OTHER SEASONS becomes NOTES; STATUS HISTORY stays.

It seems like there are two invites for some reason. There are two invite sections in W2-01. — DONE. There were: an EVENTS card AND a purple card headed WHAT WE HAVE SAID that was actually the player's own 53-row attendance table with its heading renamed over it, because rebuildCard failed silently. One events section now, and the helpers throw.

W2-02 seems to be not recruitment. It seems to be something else... It's showing the roster instead of the recruit page on its proposed pages. If we deleted W2-02 and W2-03, just the screens, and just left it with this third screen, would anything be missed? — RESOLVED: both old screens deleted. W2-02 is rebuilt as the one screen that covers what they would have shown between them: the record with the ask answered and the status field open for editing. W2-03 is gone entirely and the workflow now has two screens.

prospect_status ships six values - identified, engaged, committed, converted, lapsed, declined. The approved seven-value ladder renames two, adds void and is a frozen-model change: a new type plus a data migration, with the Recruits audience derivation and two check constraints in the blast radius.
The recruits audience group is shipped in audience-selection.ts under D46 and is restricted to recruitment events; W10 retains it.
scheduleEventLadder inserts a reminder job for every invitation with no capacity filter, so a recruit invited today receives the player escalation. The fix is a second ladder, not a silence.
countByCapacity in event-approval.ts omits recruits from the approval audit counts, so an operator approving a recruitment event is not told how many recruits it reaches.
The shipped walk-up path mints a person with no interactive duplicate check, wider than Task 09's coach-only LAN-110 exception. Recorded as drift by Task 09 amendment 4 and reconciled here.

No inbound message is captured anywhere - the webhook parses only statuses[] - and rsvp_source 'channel_reply' is an enum value no code path writes. A reply is therefore not an available signal without new work.

read and sent arrive and are stored verbatim in delivery_callbacks but map to nothing, because widening delivery_outcome is a frozen-model change. Using them as signals is a model decision, not an integration.
The core four only, no new capability minted. Sharpest at the flip, and it governs every operator surface in the mission.
Every walk-up is a recruit, and walk-up capture stays on every event type for anyone taking attendance.
One flat recruitment status of seven values, with on-the-board as a display rule over that one field.
Copy the Roster board where copying works; person details then recruitment details; one line per recruit; event columns appended at the right end.
The QR points at our own page on our own domain - they are signing in to the club's application, not a form somewhere else.
Brian: 'Recruits can get in 3 or 4 ways, but they can get off in several ways.' The exits are load-bearing because every walk-up enters the funnel.
Never harsh replaces never chased. Its home surface is the operator's follow-up workflow; it constrains the event workflows and is swept for across the whole system as an invariant.
identified, engaged, committed, then joined confirmed as the spine of the ladder.
The flip to joined interrupts with a confirmation, joined means a season membership exists, the roster shows they joined this season, and onboarding opens.
Recruitment's own board for recruits only, modelled after the roster board.
What the QR page does is explicitly undecided and is designed inside its workflow; the own-domain constraint from 2026-08-28 stands.
W3 removed 2026-08-31. Channel registration is this mission's and is its own flow; the flow is machinery, and the machinery is administered in W10.

W3 removed 2026-08-31. The named sequence is the definition of what the club sends and when, which is W10's cycle administration. Its templates already moved to W10-03 when Brian folded W3 on the same day.
One event may carry players and recruits, and each is chased on its own terms. Brian: 'they get set the invite once and maybe a polite follow-up... it needs to be a totally separate thing.'

The board and the record carry the shipped roster board's structure, grouping and colour language rather than reinventing them. Brian: 'similar structures... and similar colors, if we can keep them consistent.'
The walk-up flow is walked end to end and reworked for clarity; departure from the shipped screen is expected rather than needing justification.
Scan, form, submit, and the submission lands them in the community group. The detail is still open by Brian's own word: 'I think I want to talk more about how that works there.'

A recruit signing themselves in is told they are already in the list rather than silently parked. Brian: 'If their name is already there, they go, Oh, you've already done this.' What the self-serve door cannot resolve still goes to W8.
The recruit-stage ask is a form minted for that recruit and linked to their person, sent to them rather than published.
Recruits are treated differently from players on the attendance sheet, and who showed up reads back onto the recruit's row as a signal.
Leaving the board is a status change on the one flat field, and the board resorts. There is no separate removal mechanism. Brian: 'A moves statuses, and then the board resorts, more or less.'

A recruit sees only the public details of an event - never attendance, never who else was invited or answered, never roster or member data. Recorded as invariant 8 in 01-overview.md and drawn as the recruit-facing half of W11, which is thin enough not to need a workflow of its own.
The recruit follow-up surface belongs to this mission and is not deferred to Mission 7's message-and-flag direction. Mission 7 may inherit from it.

areas.belongs: Every stage change, flip and correction is an attributable act on personal data.
areas.invariant: Every recruitment state change, flip, correction and message is attributable and audited, and nothing about a recruit is destroyed to make the board tidy.
areas.reason: A property of every workflow rather than one actor's journey.

areas.name: Proactive sourcing as a first-class path
areas.belongs: Brian's note: the club finds people and reaches out, which the four-door framing under-serves.
areas.reason: The manual-add door is where sourcing lands, drawn as a real journey rather than a fallback.

areas.name: The WhatsApp group connection as a tracked outcome
areas.belongs: Brian named it; Task 08 row 8 puts channel presence here.
areas.reason: Recorded as presence on the recruit's record. The observability research shows group membership is not observable through the Cloud API, so it is operator-recorded, never watched.

areas.name: Signals
areas.belongs: Brian: 'We want to get as many signals as we can on the recruit.'
areas.reason: The set is enumerated from the 2026-08-28 research and approved as the board's columns, so Brian approves actual columns rather than an abstraction.

areas.name: The recruitment board as its own board
areas.belongs: Brian's 2026-08-28 and 2026-08-31 words; a list beside the roster is not what he asked for.
areas.reason: Recruitment's own board for recruits only, modelled after the roster board.

areas.name: Notes people take
areas.belongs: Brian made notes first-class; Task 09 keeps commitment signals as prose, never scored.
areas.reason: Notes live on the recruit's record and surface on the board; never scored, never ranked.

areas.name: Layering onto Mission 5's surfaces as its own section
areas.belongs: Mission 5's surfaces shipped at the baseline and this mission layers onto them.
areas.reason: The board is built like the roster board and copies it where copying works.

areas.name: The board's shape is the attendance table, for recruits
areas.belongs: Brian's own analogy for how the board reads: one line per recruit, columns appended per event.
areas.reason: Event columns append at the right end, headed by a compact handle, showing invited, answered and attended.

areas.name: Recruitment-event attendance as a first-class signal
areas.belongs: Turnout is what a recruitment event is for, and Task 09 D8 makes attendance the count.
areas.reason: Recruits on top, everyone else below, walk-ups captured into the flow.

areas.name: The signal research sprint
areas.belongs: Brian commissioned it at Stage 1 to settle what the platform can honestly observe.
areas.reason: Run and recorded at evidence/2026-08-28-signal-observability.md; its output is the signal set approved with W1's columns.

areas.name: Conservative observability default
areas.belongs: Brian's rule for the gap between what we wish we saw and what we can see.
areas.invariant: Where a signal is not established as readable, the mission assumes it is not, and no stage, display or decision depends on it.
areas.reason: A standing rule over every signal rather than a journey; it is what made the WhatsApp community-join door collapse.

areas.name: Operator-initiated outreach is permitted and recorded
areas.belongs: Brian's 2026-08-28 note, sharpened by the 2026-08-31 amendment into a first-class surface.
areas.reason: Outreach leaves the app, so it is recorded as a matter of course rather than logged by hand.

areas.name: A delayed recruit-stage ask
areas.belongs: Brian described it roughly a day after capture rather than riding the welcome.
areas.reason: The timing is the one open owner decision inside W7; the recommendation is a day later as its own message.

areas.name: Loosey-goosey as a design constraint
areas.belongs: Brian's framing: recruitment is not a rigid process and the product must not force one.
areas.invariant: Nothing about a recruit is scored, ranked, or advanced automatically by a computed value, and no step is mandatory in an order the club has to obey.
areas.reason: A constraint on how every workflow is designed rather than a journey of its own.

areas.name: Where the messaging machinery lives and how the cycle is administered
areas.belongs: Brian: 'how that message gets sent out, where that machinery lives... I'm not sure where.'
areas.reason: Mission 4 owns transport and scheduler; recruitment owns what it sends, when, and who may change it.

areas.name: The operator's follow-up surface
areas.belongs: Added by the never-harsh amendment; Mission 5 sends nothing and Mission 7's message-and-flag direction is aimed at members.
areas.reason: Composing and sending a polite message from wherever the operator already is, quickly and with good default wording. Confirmed as this mission's on 2026-08-31 against the Authority Manifest's Mission 7 candidate home; Mission 7 inherits rather than owns.
